events.title: FOMC Member Bowman Speaks
notes: Good morning. 1 I would like to thank our hosts, the Banco Central do Brasil, the Association of Supervisors of Banks of the Americas (ASBA), the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), and the Financial Stability Institute, for bringing us together.
Today, I will discuss three ways in which modernizing our supervision and regulatory frameworks can enhance our ability to be effective.

The review validated that supervisors identified the bank's fundamental vulnerabilities well before its failure. 2 Those vulnerabilities included substantial interest rate risk, a highly concentrated and predominantly uninsured deposit base, and inadequate preparedness to meet liquidity demands.
While interest rate risk was discussed, the approach criticized how the bank measured the risk but did not direct the bank to reduce it.

Our priorities should be to ensure supervisors are trained to identify and focus attention on material risks, enable timely decisionmaking and clear accountability, and establish a regulatory framework that encourages innovation without compromising safety and soundness.

noteSrc.title: Bowman, Modernizing Banking Supervision: A Shared Agenda for the Americas
